target_claim: In the converse direction of the characterization, the proof splits into the two cases 'p \preceq q' and 'p \preceq a and a \preceq q'. The second case hypothesis is not the theorem's second disjunct (which is 'p \preceq a and b \preceq q'), so (i) the case analysis does not cover all instances the theorem requires, and (ii) the lines immediately derived from it ('b \preceq' q', hence 'b \preceq'^+ q') do not follow from the stated hypothesis.
source_quote: Suppose instead that $p \preceq a$ and $a \preceq q$.
